=== Put: Sixteen Hands ===

CARDS. A deck of 52 cards: 4 copies of each value from 1 to 13. Value 13 is a Three (highest), 12 a Two, 11 an Ace, 10 a King, 9 a Queen, 8 a Jack, 7 a Ten, 6 a Nine, 5 an Eight, 4 a Seven, 3 a Six, 2 a Five and 1 a Four (lowest). There are no suits. In any trick the higher value wins, and equal values tie the trick, which then belongs to no one.

SETUP. Both players start with a score of 0. The match is exactly 16 hands. Seat 1 leads in odd-numbered hands and seat 2 leads in even-numbered hands. The other seat is the responder.

EACH HAND, in this order:
1. Reset. The full deck is restored and shuffled; hands, played cards, calls, responses, trick counts, the stake and the folded marker are cleared.
2. Deal. 3 cards to each player. Each player sees only their own cards.
3. Lead. The leader chooses one of their cards and plays it face up.
4. The lead is announced to both players.
5. Answer. Having seen the lead, the responder chooses one of their cards and plays it face up.
6. Trick 1. The higher card wins trick 1; an equal pair is a tie. The result is announced.
7. Put window. Each player privately chooses Put or Check, without seeing the other's choice.
8. Both calls are announced.
9. Reply. Only if exactly one player chose Put: the player who chose Check now chooses See or Fold. If both chose Put, the Put counts as seen. If both chose Check, there is no Put and no reply is asked. The stake is 4 if a Put was seen (by See or by both Putting), 1 if both Checked.
10. Fold. If the Checker folds, the player who Put scores 1 point and the hand ends there: no further tricks are played and the remaining cards are not shown. If the Checker Sees, the hand is played out.
11. Trick 2. Each player automatically plays the higher of their two remaining cards. Compared as in trick 1.
12. Trick 3. Each player automatically plays their last card. Compared as in trick 1.
13. Reveal. All cards and each player's number of tricks won are shown.
14. Hand scoring. A player who won at least 2 of the 3 tricks scores the stake (1 or 4). If neither player won 2 tricks, because of tied tricks, no one scores.
15. After hand 16 the match ends; otherwise the next hand begins.

There is no talk phase. After 16 hands, the player with the higher total score wins. If the totals are equal, the match is a draw (the win is shared).

In any trick the higher value wins, and equal values tie the trick, which then belongs to no one.

SETUP. Both players start with a score of 0. The match is exactly 16 hands. Seat 1 leads in odd-numbered hands and seat 2 leads in even-numbered hands. The other seat is the responder.

EACH HAND, in this order:
1. Reset. The full deck is restored and shuffled; hands, played cards, calls, responses, trick counts, the stake and the folded marker are cleared.
2. Deal. 3 cards to each player. Each player sees only their own cards.
3. Lead. The leader chooses one of their cards and plays it face up.
4. The lead is announced to both players.
5. Answer. Having seen the lead, the responder chooses one of their cards and plays it face up.
6. Trick 1. The higher card wins trick 1; an equal pair is a tie. The result is announced.
7. Put window. Each player privately chooses Put or Check, without seeing the other's choice.
8. Both calls are announced.
9. Reply. Only if exactly one player chose Put: the player who chose Check now chooses See or Fold. If both chose Put, the Put counts as seen. If both chose Check, there is no Put and no reply is asked. The stake is 4 if a Put was seen (by See or by both Putting), 1 if both Checked.
10. Fold. If the Checker folds, the player who Put scores 1 point and the hand ends there: no further tricks are played and the remaining cards are not shown. If the Checker Sees, the hand is played out.
11. Trick 2. Each player automatically plays the higher of their two remaining cards. Compared as in trick 1.
12. Trick 3. Each player automatically plays their last card. Compared as in trick 1.
13. Reveal. All cards and each player's number of tricks won are shown.
14. Hand scoring. A player who won at least 2 of the 3 tricks scores the stake (1 or 4). If neither player won 2 tricks, because of tied tricks, no one scores.
15. After hand 16 the match ends; otherwise the next hand begins.

=== Put: Sixteen Hands ===

CARDS. A deck of 52 cards: 4 copies of each value from 1 to 13. Value 13 is a Three (highest), 12 a Two, 11 an Ace, 10 a King, 9 a Queen, 8 a Jack, 7 a Ten, 6 a Nine, 5 an Eight, 4 a Seven, 3 a Six, 2 a Five and 1 a Four (lowest). There are no suits. In any trick the higher value wins, and equal values tie the trick, which then belongs to no one.

SETUP. Both players start with a score of 0. The match is exactly 16 hands. Seat 1 leads in odd-numbered hands and seat 2 leads in even-numbered hands. The other seat is the responder.

EACH HAND, in this order:
1. Reset. The full deck is restored and shuffled; hands, played cards, calls, responses, trick counts, the stake and the folded marker are cleared.
2. Deal. 3 cards to each player. Each player sees only their own cards.
3. Lead. The leader chooses one of their cards and plays it face up.
4. The lead is announced to both players.
5. Answer. Having seen the lead, the responder chooses one of their cards and plays it face up.
6. Trick 1. The higher card wins trick 1; an equal pair is a tie. The result is announced.
7. Put window. Each player privately chooses Put or Check, without seeing the other's choice.
8. Both calls are announced.
9. Reply. Only if exactly one player chose Put: the player who chose Check now chooses See or Fold. If both chose Put, the Put counts as seen. If both chose Check, there is no Put and no reply is asked. The stake is 4 if a Put was seen (by See or by both Putting), 1 if both Checked.
10. Fold. If the Checker folds, the player who Put scores 1 point and the hand ends there: no further tricks are played and the remaining cards are not shown. If the Checker Sees, the hand is played out.
11. Trick 2. Each player automatically plays the higher of their two remaining cards. Compared as in trick 1.
12. Trick 3. Each player automatically plays their last card. Compared as in trick 1.
13. Reveal. All cards and each player's number of tricks won are shown.
14. Hand scoring. A player who won at least 2 of the 3 tricks scores the stake (1 or 4). If neither player won 2 tricks, because of tied tricks, no one scores.
15. After hand 16 the match ends; otherwise the next hand begins.

There is no talk phase. After 16 hands, the player with the higher total score wins. If the totals are equal, the match is a draw (the win is shared).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

The match lasts exactly 16 hands. Both players start with a score of 0.

Each round runs in this order: reset → deal → your hand → lead → announce the lead → answer → trick 1 → put window → announce the calls → reply to a lone put → stake → fold scoring → trick 2 → trick 3 → reveal → hand scoring → end check.

  reply_to_a_lone_put answer with one of: See, Fold

  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,

  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

EACH HAND, in this order:

You are reviewing a game that has finished. You were not a player. You are shown everything: the messages the table was told, every move, and each player's private thinking at every move, which no other player ever saw. Each move carries the notes its game asked for, under their own names. The usual ones are:

  plan     what they meant to do over the coming turns
  reason   why they made that move
  predict  what they expected their opponents to do
  adjust   how they changed their own strategy because of that

Write two things.

First, a summary of the whole game as it unfolded: the turning points, the moves that decided it, and how it ended. Concrete: name seats, rounds and numbers.

Second, a review of each player. Judge their play, not their luck. For each one, compare their predictions with what their opponents were actually thinking and actually did: were they right, and did they see it in time? Did their adjustments follow from their predictions, and did their moves follow from their reasons? Point out their best and worst moves. Then score their play from 1 to 10, where 1 is aimless or self-defeating and 10 is sharp, well read and well executed. A player can lose and still score well, or win and score badly.

A player who gave no reasons, predictions or adjustments is judged on their moves alone; say that their thinking was not recorded.

Refer to each player by seat, and as "they".

THE GAME
CARDS. A deck of 52 cards: 4 copies of each value from 1 to 13. Value 13 is a Three (highest), 12 a Two, 11 an Ace, 10 a King, 9 a Queen, 8 a Jack, 7 a Ten, 6 a Nine, 5 an Eight, 4 a Seven, 3 a Six, 2 a Five and 1 a Four (lowest). There are no suits. In any trick the higher value wins, and equal values tie the trick, which then belongs to no one.

SETUP. Both players start with a score of 0. The match is exactly 16 hands. Seat 1 leads in odd-numbered hands and seat 2 leads in even-numbered hands. The other seat is the responder.

EACH HAND, in this order:
1. Reset. The full deck is restored and shuffled; hands, played cards, calls, responses, trick counts, the stake and the folded marker are cleared.
2. Deal. 3 cards to each player. Each player sees only their own cards.
3. Lead. The leader chooses one of their cards and plays it face up.
4. The lead is announced to both players.
5. Answer. Having seen the lead, the responder chooses one of their cards and plays it face up.
6. Trick 1. The higher card wins trick 1; an equal pair is a tie. The result is announced.
7. Put window. Each player privately chooses Put or Check, without seeing the other's choice.
8. Both calls are announced.
9. Reply. Only if exactly one player chose Put: the player who chose Check now chooses See or Fold. If both chose Put, the Put counts as seen. If both chose Check, there is no Put and no reply is asked. The stake is 4 if a Put was seen (by See or by both Putting), 1 if both Checked.
10. Fold. If the Checker folds, the player who Put scores 1 point and the hand ends there: no further tricks are played and the remaining cards are not shown. If the Checker Sees, the hand is played out.
11. Trick 2. Each player automatically plays the higher of their two remaining cards. Compared as in trick 1.
12. Trick 3. Each player automatically plays their last card. Compared as in trick 1.
13. Reveal. All cards and each player's number of tricks won are shown.
14. Hand scoring. A player who won at least 2 of the 3 tricks scores the stake (1 or 4). If neither player won 2 tricks, because of tied tricks, no one scores.
15. After hand 16 the match ends; otherwise the next hand begins.

There is no talk phase. After 16 hands, the player with the higher total score wins. If the totals are equal, the match is a draw (the win is shared).
